58: ### Pattern
59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.

61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.

68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.

72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 114 over the five docs a Level 2 scaffold creates.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.

84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.

91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
92: |-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |

404: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
405: 
406: ### ADR-001: Reuse the existing token and gate by the template stamp
407: 
408: **Status**: Accepted
409: 
410: **Context**: The token `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` is already an error in the validator and is already documented in `template-style-guide.md` section 3. A flag or an environment switch would need setting in every repo, and an external repo could not be expected to set it.
411: 
412: **Decision**: No new grammar. A doc stamped v2.3 or later gets the Draft lifecycle. Any other doc keeps its old verdict.
413: 
414: **Consequences**:
415: - The gate turns on by itself for each new scaffold and never for an old packet.
416: - A hand-written doc that copies a v2.3 stamp opts itself in. That is the intended meaning of the stamp.
417: 
418: **Alternatives Rejected**:
419: - An environment flag: it would have to be set in every external repo, and an unset flag is silent.
420: - Gating by packet creation date: dates are fragile across copies and renames, and the stamp already travels with the doc.
421: 
422: ### ADR-002: Draft means the word Draft, and a warning does not fail strict
423: 
424: **Status**: Accepted
425: 
426: **Context**: Planning commits must keep passing, as the rule `SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED` already allows for a Draft. Other status words, such as Planned or In Progress, are real work states where a leftover hint is a defect.
427: 
428: **Decision**: Only the exact word Draft defers a token to a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. The orchestrator already treats a warning as advice, so strict still passes with warnings.
429: 
430: **Consequences**:
431: - A packet marked In Progress with tokens fails, which is the point of the gate.
432: - A packet with the status `Draft (phase 3)` counts as not Draft. The author writes `Draft`.
433: 
434: **Alternatives Rejected**:
435: - Treat every non-Complete status as Draft: a weak model that sets In Progress could then leave every hint for ever.
436: 
437: ### ADR-003: Record two defects in the post-edit scanner and leave the file alone
438: 
439: **Status**: Accepted
440: 
441: **Context**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh` is the broad scan the post-edit hook runs. Two defects were observed with probe files. It skips only the lines that start a code fence and not the lines between fences, so a bracketed hint inside a fenced block exits 1. Its bracket class has no colon, so a line that holds a value token after the word Priority exits 0. After this phase the hook therefore stops reporting unfilled tokens in new packets.
442: 
443: **Decision**: This phase does not edit that file. It is a different script from the rule being changed, with a different caller, and the fix for the colon blind spot would change the hook verdict for existing packets that hold text such as `[SOURCE: ...]`. The conductor records the two defects in `goal.md` section 4 as follow-up rows with these probe commands, and raises them to the operator.
444: 
445: **Consequences**:
446: - The validator warning is the only signal for a Draft packet until the scanner is fixed.
447: - No existing hook verdict changes in this phase.
448: 
449: **Alternatives Rejected**:
450: - Add the colon to the bracket class here: it changes which existing packets the hook flags, with no test covering the scanner.
451: 
452: ### ADR-004: Convert with a script and keep the scaffolder's own placeholders
453: 
454: **Status**: Accepted
455: 
456: **Context**: By the frozen regex the five templates hold 254 bracketed hints. Of those, 214 are to convert, 38 are texts that `create.sh` replaces or strips and 2 sit inside an inline code span. A hand edit by a weak model would miss some and corrupt others.
457: 
458: **Decision**: `convert_hints.py` converts by the frozen rule and prints how many it changed. Counts before and after, and the list of bare texts left, are checked by commands.
459: 
460: **Consequences**:
461: - The result is the same on every run, and a second run changes nothing.
462: - A hint that the rule keeps but a later phase wants as a token needs a rule change, not a hand edit.
463: 
464: **Alternatives Rejected**:
465: - Convert by hand: error prone at this size.
466: - Convert the scaffolder's own placeholders too: every scaffold would then keep a token for the feature name and the date.
467: 
468: ### ADR-005: Accept the era report flip and raise it to the operator
469: 
470: **Status**: Accepted
471: 
472: **Context**: `template-version-parity.vitest.ts` forces the manifest version to equal the template stamp, so the manifest must say v2.3. `repo-era.mjs` marks a document `legacy` when its stamp differs from the manifest. Run against this repository with the two manifests, the report went from 16871 `new` and 2374 `legacy` markers to 1421 `new` and 17824 `legacy`. `/doctor:update check` treats a `legacy` count above zero as a pre-v4 signal, so a repo with none today would start showing it. The validator verdict for every packet is unchanged.
473: 
474: **Decision**: This phase does not edit `repo-era.mjs` or the doctor command. It records the measured counts and three options in `goal.md` section 4 and in the closing report: accept the flip, teach the era report that v2.2 is still a current stamp for old docs, or hold the manifest bump until the doctor signal is adjusted.
475: 
476: **Consequences**:
477: - The operator decides before a release carries the new templates to external repos.
478: - Decision D-b is met for the validator and open for the doctor signal.
479: 
480: **Alternatives Rejected**:
481: - Skip the manifest bump: the parity test would fail.
482: - Edit the era report here: it is outside the frozen file list and changes a doctor contract.
483: 
484: ### ADR-006: Record the upgrade-level token copy and leave it
485: 
486: **Status**: Accepted
487: 
488: **Context**: `upgrade-level.sh` renders sections from the templates into an older doc and does not touch the doc's template stamp. After this phase those sections arrive as tokens inside a doc that still says v2.2, and a token in a v2.2 doc is an error. Before this phase the same upgrade inserted bare hints that validated clean.
489: 
490: **Decision**: Not fixed here. The conductor records it as an operator item with the probe in `goal.md` section 4. The full suite includes `upgrade-level-sections.vitest.ts` and `test-upgrade-level.sh`, and `tasks.md` T017 reports whether either changed.
491: 
492: **Consequences**:
493: - An operator who upgrades an old packet to a higher level must fill the new sections or set the stamp.
494: - No existing packet changes, because the upgrade is an explicit action.
495: 
496: **Alternatives Rejected**:
497: - Stamp the upgraded doc v2.3: it would put a whole older doc under the new contract without anyone choosing that.
498: 
499: ### ADR-007: Update both implementations together and prove them with one test
500: 
501: **Status**: Accepted
502: 
503: **Context**: The orchestrator decides every real verdict. The shell rule is a mirror that a harness still drives. The two already differ in the docs they read.
504: 
505: **Decision**: Both get the same lifecycle in this phase. The shell rule reads `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` and `goal.md` only when they carry the gate stamp, so older docs are scanned exactly as before. One test file runs both on the same folder and compares the result.
506: 
507: **Consequences**:
508: - For a doc with the gate stamp the two agree on pass, warn and error.
509: - The old difference in the docs read stays for older docs and is listed in `validation-rules.md`.
510: 
511: **Alternatives Rejected**:
512: - Update only the orchestrator: the mirror would drift on day one.

56: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
57: 
58: ### Pattern
59: A stamp-gated lifecycle. The template stamp says which contract a doc was written under. The validator keeps the old strict verdict for any doc without the new stamp and applies the Draft lifecycle only to docs that carry it.
60: 
61: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
62: 
63: - `validate.sh` runs the compiled `runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`, never the shell rules, for the rule `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`. The orchestrator lists it in `nativeRuleIds`, and `runRegistryShellRules` skips every rule in that set. The proof is the wording: a v2.3 scaffold validated in a scratch copy printed `unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet`, which is the new orchestrator message, and not the shell message.
64: - `validate.sh` exits 3 with the text `compiled validation orchestrator is stale` when `runtime/dist` is older than its source. So the TypeScript edit is invisible until `npm run build` runs under `runtime/`.
65: - `rules/check-placeholders.sh` still matters. The harness `runtime/cli/tests/test-validation-extended.sh` sources it in the category `Individual Rule: PLACEHOLDER_FILLED (check-placeholders.sh)`, and its header says it mirrors the orchestrator.
66: - A warning does not fail strict. The orchestrator sets `passed: summary.errors === 0`.
67: - `create.sh` function `finalize_scaffold_templates` replaces `[NAME]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]`, `[Feature Name]` and `[###-feature-name]` and strips ` [template:...]` with `perl`. Function `ensure_template_source_near_top` moves the stamp line below the frontmatter. The stamp text, including its version, comes from the template.
68: - `templates/spec-kit-docs.json` lists a version per template, and `runtime/cli/tests/template-version-parity.vitest.ts` fails when a manifest version differs from the template stamp.
69: - `runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts` renders these templates and compares them with `runtime/cli/tests/snapshots/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts.snap`. Without `-u` it fails after conversion on four tests.
70: - The orchestrator reads every authored doc that is present. The shell rule reads only `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `decision-record.md`. This difference exists today and the plan keeps it for older docs (ADR-007).
71: 
72: ### Frozen definitions
73: 
74: **Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 114 over the five docs a Level 2 scaffold creates.
75: 
76: **Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
77: 1. A line inside a fenced code block.
78: 2. Text inside an inline code span.
79: 3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
80: 4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
81: 5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.
82: 
83: **Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.
84: 
85: **Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.
86: 
87: **Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.

91: | Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |

93: | Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
94: | Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |

404: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
405: 
406: ### ADR-001: Reuse the existing token and gate by the template stamp
407: 
408: **Status**: Accepted
409: 
410: **Context**: The token `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` is already an error in the validator and is already documented in `template-style-guide.md` section 3. A flag or an environment switch would need setting in every repo, and an external repo could not be expected to set it.
411: 
412: **Decision**: No new grammar. A doc stamped v2.3 or later gets the Draft lifecycle. Any other doc keeps its old verdict.
413: 
414: **Consequences**:
415: - The gate turns on by itself for each new scaffold and never for an old packet.
416: - A hand-written doc that copies a v2.3 stamp opts itself in. That is the intended meaning of the stamp.
417: 
418: **Alternatives Rejected**:
419: - An environment flag: it would have to be set in every external repo, and an unset flag is silent.
420: - Gating by packet creation date: dates are fragile across copies and renames, and the stamp already travels with the doc.
421: 
422: ### ADR-002: Draft means the word Draft, and a warning does not fail strict
423: 
424: **Status**: Accepted
425: 
426: **Context**: Planning commits must keep passing, as the rule `SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED` already allows for a Draft. Other status words, such as Planned or In Progress, are real work states where a leftover hint is a defect.
427: 
428: **Decision**: Only the exact word Draft defers a token to a warning. Every other value, and a missing Status row, makes it an error. The orchestrator already treats a warning as advice, so strict still passes with warnings.
429: 
430: **Consequences**:
431: - A packet marked In Progress with tokens fails, which is the point of the gate.
432: - A packet with the status `Draft (phase 3)` counts as not Draft. The author writes `Draft`.
433: 
434: **Alternatives Rejected**:
435: - Treat every non-Complete status as Draft: a weak model that sets In Progress could then leave every hint for ever.
436: 
437: ### ADR-003: Record two defects in the post-edit scanner and leave the file alone
438: 
439: **Status**: Accepted
440: 
441: **Context**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh` is the broad scan the post-edit hook runs. Two defects were observed with probe files. It skips only the lines that start a code fence and not the lines between fences, so a bracketed hint inside a fenced block exits 1. Its bracket class has no colon, so a line that holds a value token after the word Priority exits 0. After this phase the hook therefore stops reporting unfilled tokens in new packets.
442: 
443: **Decision**: This phase does not edit that file. It is a different script from the rule being changed, with a different caller, and the fix for the colon blind spot would change the hook verdict for existing packets that hold text such as `[SOURCE: ...]`. The conductor records the two defects in `goal.md` section 4 as follow-up rows with these probe commands, and raises them to the operator.
444: 
445: **Consequences**:
446: - The validator warning is the only signal for a Draft packet until the scanner is fixed.
447: - No existing hook verdict changes in this phase.
448: 
449: **Alternatives Rejected**:
450: - Add the colon to the bracket class here: it changes which existing packets the hook flags, with no test covering the scanner.
451: 
452: ### ADR-004: Convert with a script and keep the scaffolder's own placeholders
453: 
454: **Status**: Accepted
455: 
456: **Context**: By the frozen regex the five templates hold 254 bracketed hints. Of those, 214 are to convert, 38 are texts that `create.sh` replaces or strips and 2 sit inside an inline code span. A hand edit by a weak model would miss some and corrupt others.
457: 
458: **Decision**: `convert_hints.py` converts by the frozen rule and prints how many it changed. Counts before and after, and the list of bare texts left, are checked by commands.
459: 
460: **Consequences**:
461: - The result is the same on every run, and a second run changes nothing.
462: - A hint that the rule keeps but a later phase wants as a token needs a rule change, not a hand edit.
463: 
464: **Alternatives Rejected**:
465: - Convert by hand: error prone at this size.
466: - Convert the scaffolder's own placeholders too: every scaffold would then keep a token for the feature name and the date.
467: 
468: ### ADR-005: Accept the era report flip and raise it to the operator
469: 
470: **Status**: Accepted
471: 
472: **Context**: `template-version-parity.vitest.ts` forces the manifest version to equal the template stamp, so the manifest must say v2.3. `repo-era.mjs` marks a document `legacy` when its stamp differs from the manifest. Run against this repository with the two manifests, the report went from 16871 `new` and 2374 `legacy` markers to 1421 `new` and 17824 `legacy`. `/doctor:update check` treats a `legacy` count above zero as a pre-v4 signal, so a repo with none today would start showing it. The validator verdict for every packet is unchanged.
473: 
474: **Decision**: This phase does not edit `repo-era.mjs` or the doctor command. It records the measured counts and three options in `goal.md` section 4 and in the closing report: accept the flip, teach the era report that v2.2 is still a current stamp for old docs, or hold the manifest bump until the doctor signal is adjusted.
475: 
476: **Consequences**:
477: - The operator decides before a release carries the new templates to external repos.
478: - Decision D-b is met for the validator and open for the doctor signal.
479: 
480: **Alternatives Rejected**:
481: - Skip the manifest bump: the parity test would fail.
482: - Edit the era report here: it is outside the frozen file list and changes a doctor contract.
483: 
484: ### ADR-006: Record the upgrade-level token copy and leave it
485: 
486: **Status**: Accepted
487: 
488: **Context**: `upgrade-level.sh` renders sections from the templates into an older doc and does not touch the doc's template stamp. 52: ### Phase 3: versioned-placeholder-gate
53: 
54: When it runs, this phase turns 214 authoring hints in the five core templates into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` tokens and stamps the templates v2.3. A packet scaffolded from them then fails strict validation once its Status leaves Draft with a hint still unfilled, and only warns while it is Draft. Packets with an older stamp keep exactly the verdict they have today. The planning session measured this against a scratch copy of the repository: strict results over 4,766 folders came out identical before and after, and the new test failed first and went red under all three scripted breaks.
55: 
56: The planning session also found three side effects it does not fix. They are listed under Known Limitations and in `goal.md` section 4 as operator items.
57:

59: 
60: | File | Action | Purpose |
61: |------|--------|---------|

68: ## How It Was Delivered
69: 
70: Not delivered yet. The conductor runs `tasks.md` T001 to T021 itself with saved tools, and no worker model edits a file. The one model call is a read-only review through `cli-codex` with `gpt-6-luna`. The phase makes no commit, because the operator commits.
71: <!-- /ANCHOR:how-delivered -->
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: <!-- ANCHOR:decisions -->
76: ## Key Decisions
77: 
78: | Decision | Why |
79: |----------|-----|
80: | Reuse the existing `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` token | The validator already knows it, so no new grammar needs teaching |
81: | Gate on the v2.3 stamp and the exact Status word Draft | A stamp keeps every existing packet on its old rule, and a warning does not fail strict |
82: | Convert by script and keep the scaffolder's own texts | `create.sh` replaces some hints at scaffold time, and a hand edit could break that |
83: | Update the orchestrator and the shell rule together | `validate.sh` runs the orchestrator and a test compares the shell rule with it |
84: | Record the scanner defects, the era flip and the upgrade-level copy | Fixing them is outside the frozen file list |
85: <!-- /ANCHOR:decisions -->

105: 2. **The post-edit scanner is blind in two ways.** It exits 1 on a hint inside a fenced block and exits 0 on a token that has a colon. This phase records both and fixes neither.

finalize_scaffold_templates() {
    local folder_path="$1"
    local packet_pointer="$2"
    local feature_name="$3"
    local doc_level="${4:-$DOC_LEVEL}"
    local safe_packet_pointer
    safe_packet_pointer="$(slugify_token "$packet_pointer")"
    [[ -n "$safe_packet_pointer" ]] || safe_packet_pointer="$packet_pointer"
    local escaped_feature_name
    escaped_feature_name="$(escape_template_value "$feature_name")"
    local today now_iso
    today="$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%d")"
    now_iso="$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")"

    # Contract documents may sit one directory down (research/research.md,
    # review/review-report.md); they carry the same placeholders as root docs.
    local md_file
    for md_file in "$folder_path"/*.md "$folder_path"/*/*.md; do
        [[ -f "$md_file" ]] || continue
        [[ "$md_file" == "$folder_path/scratch/"* ]] && continue
        PACKET_POINTER="scaffold/$safe_packet_pointer" RAW_PACKET_POINTER="$packet_pointer" FEATURE_NAME="$escaped_feature_name" TODAY="$today" NOW_ISO="$now_iso" DOC_LEVEL="$doc_level" perl -0pi -e '
            s{\[NAME\]}{$ENV{FEATURE_NAME}}g;
            s{\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: feature-name\]}{$ENV{FEATURE_NAME}}g;
            s{\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: YYYY-MM-DD\]}{$ENV{TODAY}}g;
            s/\[###-feature-name\]/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/000-feature-name/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/packet_pointer: "[^"]+"/packet_pointer: "$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}"/g;
            s/system-spec-kit\/templates\/level-1/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/system-spec-kit\/templates\/level-2/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/system-spec-kit\/templates\/level-3\+/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/system-spec-kit\/templates\/level-3/$ENV{PACKET_POINTER}/g;
            s/\| \*\*Spec Folder\*\* \| scaffold\/([^|]+) \|/| **Spec Folder** | $ENV{RAW_PACKET_POINTER} |/g;
            s/\| \*\*Level\*\* \| \[1\/2\/3\/3\+\] \|/| **Level** | $ENV{DOC_LEVEL} |/g;
            s/\[YYYY-MM-DD\]/$ENV{TODAY}/g;
            s/last_updated_at: "[^"]+"/last_updated_at: "$ENV{NOW_ISO}"/g;
            s{\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: packet-id\]}{$ENV{RAW_PACKET_POINTER}}g;
            s/\[Feature Name\]/$ENV{FEATURE_NAME}/g;
            s/ \[template:[^\]]+\]//g;
            s/session_id: "template-session"/"session_id: \"scaffold-$ENV{RAW_PACKET_POINTER}\""/eg;
        ' "$md_file"
        ensure_template_source_near_top "$md_file"
    done
}

# A checkout without a build or an install lacks the generators behind
# description.json and the derived graph metadata. The scaffold still succeeds
# without them, so each skip names the missing file and how to get it.
report_missing_generator() {
    local skipped="$1"
    local missing="$2"
    local remedy="$3"
    local target="${4:-}"
    echo "  Warning: ${skipped} skipped${target:+ for ${target}}: ${missing} is missing. ${remedy}" >&2
}

readonly BUILD_REMEDY="Run npm run build under runtime to compile it."
readonly INSTALL_REMEDY="Run npm install at the skill root, then repair-derived.cjs --folder <packet> --apply."

# Derive the graph metadata from the documents that were just written, rather
# than leaving the stub the scaffolder guessed. A scaffold that disagrees with
# its own deriver fails validation the moment it exists, which teaches an author
# that the gate is broken before they have written a line. A missing tool or a
# failed derivation warns and leaves the scaffold in place.
backfill_graph_metadata() {
    local backfill_ts="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../graph/backfill-graph-metadata.ts"
    local tsx_loader="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../../node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs"
    if [[ ! -f "$tsx_loader" ]]; then
        report_missing_generator "graph metadata derivation" "$tsx_loader" "$INSTALL_REMEDY"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ ! -f "$backfill_ts" ]]; then
        report_missing_generator "graph metadata derivation" "$backfill_ts" "Restore it from the repository."
        return 0
    fi
    local folder_path
    for folder_path in "$@"; do
        [[ -n "$folder_path" ]] || continue
        node --import "$tsx_loader" "$backfill_ts" "$folder_path" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || echo "  Warning: graph metadata derivation skipped for ${folder_path##*/}" >&2
    done
}

# A track root declares its packets in children_ids, and the pre-push gate
# blocks a commit whose list disagrees with the packets it holds. Declaring the
# new packet here keeps the two in step from the moment the packet exists. A
# track with no graph-metadata.json declares nothing, so there is nothing to do.
refresh_track_root() {
    local specs_root="$1"
    local track="$2"
    local refresh_script="$SCRIPT_DIR/refresh-track-roots.mjs"
    [[ -n "$track" && "$track" != */* && -f "$specs_root/$track/graph-metadata.json" ]] || return 0
    if [[ ! -f "$refresh_script" ]]; then
        report_missing_generator "track root refresh" "$refresh_script" "Restore it from the repository."
        return 0
    fi
    # The writer reports on stdout; stdout belongs to the --json payload.

REPO RULES.md
# REPO RULES

Repo-local operating rules. `AGENTS.md` **Gate 5 (§2)** makes reading this mandatory
before your first write of the session; this document then routes you to every rule
file that governs what you are about to do. **It is a router, not a rulebook:** it
holds no rules of its own.

---

## 1. HOW TO USE THIS

1. **Match on the action you are about to take**, not the topic of the request.
2. **Load before the action.** A rule read afterwards is a post-mortem.
3. **A file already in context is not re-read.**
4. **Every trigger that fires is loaded, not just the first.** They compose; the more
   specific wins on conflict. Three and four firing at once is the normal case, not an
   edge case.
5. **Nothing fires → `AGENTS.md` alone governs.** Do not hunt for a rule to apply.

### Precedence

| Level | Source | Can be overridden? |
|-------|--------|--------------------|
| 1 | Every `AGENTS.md` §1 hard blocker, the Four Laws, PLAN-WORKFLOW LOCK, Comment Hygiene, and every mandatory gate in §2 | No |
| 2 | An explicit, in-the-moment operator instruction | Not applicable, it is the instruction |
| 3 | These rule files, and the guidance in a skill's `SKILL.md` | Only by level 1 or 2 |
| 4 | General judgment | By anything above |

A rule file may tighten `AGENTS.md`. None relaxes a HARD BLOCK or authorizes what
`AGENTS.md` forbids. Gate 5 does not change that: it makes the **load** mandatory,
while what you load stays at level 3, the obligation to read is tier 1, the content
is not.

---

## 2. TRIGGER TABLE

| You are about to… | Load | It settles |
|-------------------|------|-----------|
| Add a file, module, class, interface, option, layer, or dependency · generalize something that works · write "flexible", "future-proof", "scalable", "extensible", "might need", "best practice", "while we're here" · add a test beyond the coverage floor | [`prevent-overengineering.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/prevent-overengineering.md) | Whether this should exist at all, and at what size |
| Touch a file outside the ask · fix something noticed in passing · change something else because it would make the fix easier · rename, reformat, or delete beyond the named area · deviate from an approved plan · decide what to do with the rest when part of the work is blocked · notice a defect, smell or stale comment outside the files in scope | [`scope-discipline.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/scope-discipline.md) | What is yours to change, and how to raise what isn't |
| Say "done", "works", "fixed", "passing", "no regressions" · report a result · quote a number · act on a tool's or sub-agent's success report · close out a turn · report a file path or command output · write a completion summary or tick something off as done | [`evidence-and-proof.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/evidence-and-proof.md) | What counts as proof, how a green run lies, what an honest close-out contains |
| Decide whether to hand work to another runtime at all · hand it to a CLI executor, sub-agent, fan-out lineage, or deep loop · compose the prompt one will act on · accept or quote what one returned · answer a judgment question from your own reading alone | [`delegation-and-orchestration.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/delegation-and-orchestration.md) | The orchestrating posture, what a brief must carry, why one model is one opinion |
| Delete, overwrite, migrate, deploy, publish, send, install · force-push or rewrite history · change a shared contract · touch auth, data, or config · make any call that leaves this machine · truncate · touch branches, tags, or reflogs | [`blast-radius.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/blast-radius.md) | Reversibility, the rollback sentence, when to stop for a yes |
| Diagnose a failure · make a red check green · attempt the same fix twice · add a special case, retry, sleep, or broadened catch · call a failure a flake, infra, or pre-existing | [`root-cause-and-debugging.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/root-cause-and-debugging.md) | Fixing the producer instead of the symptom, and when to level up to the seam |
| Answer without certainty · contradict the operator · fill a gap with a plausible guess · hit a contradiction between two things that must both be true · name a path, flag, function, version, or number you have not verified · not know while a plausible answer is available · see sources disagree, or the code contradict the spec, the docs or the operator · the operator asserts something you believe is wrong · change a checked answer after pushback or doubt, or drop an approach before it concludes | [`uncertainty-and-honesty.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/uncertainty-and-honesty.md) | Confidence bands, UNKNOWN, contradiction halts |
| Prepend a warning, caveat or disclaimer the request did not ask for · answer a narrower, "safer" or easier version of the ask · cite a rule, restriction, policy, limit or permission · decline, deflect or steer the reader off the request · open a task with an effort or timeline estimate | [`answer-the-actual-request.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/answer-the-actual-request.md) | Whether the reply answers the request that was made, and what an honest no looks like |
| Write any substantive reply · the reader says they did not follow | [`communication.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/communication.md) | How a reply reads: length, filler, and no table in a reply |
| Draft or edit any sentence a reader will read · choose a word · place a dash, colon or semicolon · split or join sentences · write a paragraph | [`communication-prose.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-prose.md) | How a sentence reads: sentence and paragraph shape, plain words, punctuation |
| Present a recommendation, a fork, or a trade-off · answer a complex or ambiguous request · start a multi-step stretch the reader cannot see inside · report what a long run found · list every option you considered | [`communication-decisions.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-decisions.md) | Verdict first, one recommended path, saying where you are going before a long stretch |
| End a turn · report work done, blocked, or partly done · end a turn while something you started is still running · ask the operator anything · end a turn on a fork or two acceptable paths · continue past a decision nobody made | [`communication-handoff.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-handoff.md) | What is the operator's to do next, what is still running and what resumes it, and when a question becomes a structured choice |
| Wire, rewire or remove a mode in a parent-hub skill · edit a hub's registry, router, `ROUTER.md`, `graph-metadata.json` or `SKILL.md` mode table · report that a mode is registered, routed, reachable or integrated · quote a per-hub gate result · create a new skill under a hub, or refactor one that already lives there | [`skill-hub-routing.md`](.skilled/repo-rules/skill-hub-routing.md) | The two routing stages, what "integrated" requires, and checking the hub you actually changed |

---

## 3. INDEX

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| [Overengineering](.skilled/repo-rules/prevent-overengineering.md) | Build the smallest thing that solves the stated problem; take a costlier move only by naming what fails at the cheaper one. |
| [Scope discipline](.skilled/repo-rules/scope-discipline.md) | The requested scope is the deliverable. Adjacent problems get named, not fixed. |
| [Evidence and proof](.skilled/repo-rules/evidence-and-proof.md) | A claim is only as strong as the observation behind it, and a receipt confirms only what could have contradicted it. Distinguish observed from derived from inferred. |
| [Delegation and orchestration](.skilled/repo-rules/delegation-and-orchestration.md) | Delegating makes you the orchestrator; brief with evidence, and no single model's verdict closes a question. |
| [Blast radius](.skilled/repo-rules/blast-radius.md) | Size effort to what the change can break; no irreversible step without a named rollback and a yes. |
| [Root cause](.skilled/repo-rules/root-cause-and-debugging.md) | Fix the producer, not the symptom; every fix names the mechanism that caused the failure. |
| [Uncertainty and honesty](.skilled/repo-rules/uncertainty-and-honesty.md) | Never fabricate; mark the confidence you actually have and halt on a contradiction. |
| [Answer the actual request](.skilled/repo-rules/answer-the-actual-request.md) | Answer the request that was made. A warning nobody asked for, a quieter version of the ask, an invented constraint, a dressed-up refusal and a stall dressed as diligence are one failure. |
| [Communication](.skilled/repo-rules/communication.md) | Write so the reader can act after one pass: no table in a reply, nothing that does not carry information. |
| [Communication prose](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-prose.md) | How a sentence reads: sentence and paragraph shape, plain words, punctuation. |
| [Communication decisions](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-decisions.md) | When the reader has to decide or act on what you found, lead with the verdict, recommend one path, and say where you are going before a long stretch of work. |
| [Communication handoff](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-handoff.md) | End every turn by naming what is now the operator's to do, in the form that lets them do it. |
| [Hub routing](.skilled/repo-rules/skill-hub-routing.md) | A hub routes in two stages, so a mode registered on one surface is not reachable, and a gate run without its hub argument reports on a hub you did not touch. |

Each file expands `AGENTS.md` and is bounded by it: where a rule file appears to
permit something `AGENTS.md` restricts, `AGENTS.md` wins and the rule file is wrong.

---

## 4. SCOPE OF THIS DOCUMENT

**In:** how to think and act, restraint, scope, evidence, risk, diagnosis, honesty,
the posture to hold when work is handed to another runtime, how the resulting reply
reads, what you may claim about wiring you have changed, and how a turn hands control
back to the operator. The delegation posture was the first widening and Delivery the
second, added when `AGENTS.md` §8 moved down. Delivery is one of two rules here whose
trigger is a whole turn rather than a specific action, the other being the handback rule,
which fires at every turn's end, and §8 keeps the two clauses that must bind even when
nothing loads.

**Out:** skill routing, workflow selection, spec-folder mechanics, and the *mechanics*
of agent and CLI dispatch: which agent, which command, which model, which flags.
Those belong to `AGENTS.md` §2 and the skills it routes to, and are deliberately
absent here so each has exactly one place to change. The line is between plumbing and
posture: how to dispatch is theirs, how to think while dispatching is ours.

**The routing carve-out, added deliberately as the third widening.** *Selecting* a
route stays Out. *Verifying wiring you changed, and what you may claim about it*, is
In; it is an evidence obligation whose subject happens to be routing. `skill-hub-routing.md`
is the one rule on this side of that line, and it carries no route-selection guidance:
the mechanics stay in the skills, and the rule points at them. A fourth widening that
admits selection itself would dissolve the boundary; this one does not.

**The ask-surface carve-out, added as the fourth widening, on an operator decision that
overrode a research refusal.** A four-iteration decision-test run returned *refuse* here:
naming a question tool per runtime reads as the "which command" family, and the paragraph
above pre-refuses a fourth widening that admits selection. The operator widened it anyway,
and what follows is the narrowing that keeps the boundary standing. *Choosing between
runtimes, agents, commands, models or flags* stays Out, unchanged. *Naming the surface that
asks the operator a question, in the runtime you are already running in*, is In. That is not
a selection, because nothing is being selected: the runtime is a given, and the rule records
which of its surfaces carries an obligation the rule already imposes. `communication-handoff.md`
is the one rule on this side of that line, its §5 is the only place a tool name appears, and
it names only what this repository confirms. A fifth widening that let a rule pick between
runtimes would be the dissolution this one avoids.

| [Evidence and proof](.skilled/repo-rules/evidence-and-proof.md) | A claim is only as strong as the observation behind it, and a receipt confirms only what could have contradicted it. Distinguish observed from derived from inferred. |

| [Blast radius](.skilled/repo-rules/blast-radius.md) | Size effort to what the change can break; no irreversible step without a named rollback and a yes. |
| [Root cause](.skilled/repo-rules/root-cause-and-debugging.md) | Fix the producer, not the symptom; every fix names the mechanism that caused the failure. |

32: # Rule: Evidence and proof
33: 
34: > Routed from [`REPO RULES.md`](../../REPO%20RULES.md). Load before making any claim someone will act on.
35: > Expands `AGENTS.md`, never overrides it. Where they appear to disagree, `AGENTS.md` wins and this file is wrong. Say so.
36: 
37: ## Fires when
38: 
39: - About to say "done", "complete", "works", "fixed", "passing", or "no regressions".
40: - About to report a result, a number, a file path, or command output.
41: - A tool, sub-agent, or reviewer reports success or a finding and you are about to act on it.
42: - About to write a completion summary, or tick anything off as done.
43: - You are closing out a turn.
44: 
45: ## The rule
46: 
47: **A claim is only as strong as the observation behind it. Every load-bearing claim
48: carries its receipt, or is explicitly labeled as inferred.**
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 1. THREE TIERS
53: 
54: | Tier | Meaning | How it must appear |
55: |------|---------|--------------------|
56: | **OBSERVED** | You ran it and read the output and exit status | Cite the receipt: the command, the `file:line`, the artifact path |
57: | **DERIVED** | Follows necessarily from something observed | Show the observation and the step from it |
58: | **INFERRED** | Plausible, unverified | Say so, and say what would confirm it |
59: 
60: Prose that mixes the three without marking them reads as if all of it were observed.
61: What to do when a claim cannot be resolved is
62: [`uncertainty-and-honesty.md`](uncertainty-and-honesty.md).
63: 
64: **A receipt confirms only what could have contradicted it.** If the claim being false would
65: have left the receipt unchanged, the receipt is not an observation of that claim. It
66: belongs in INFERRED until repaired. Four shapes recur, each with one repair.
67: A search that found nothing: demonstrate the search on a known instance of what you claim
68: is absent, or you have tested your pattern, not the claim. A read that stopped short: read
69: the span where the failure would actually print. A total carried from another analysis:
70: derive it here, at the total's own level. A match that never distinguished roles: compare
71: what the two sides are, not the digits they share. With no known instance to hand, the
72: honest output is INFERRED plus the step that would confirm it.
73: 
74: When a report leads with a cause, the cause carries its standing, and the cause-then-fix
75: order holds. Where no run confirms the cause, it is INFERRED: label it as suspected and
76: name the next check. A confirmed cause is reported as a finding with its receipt. There
77: is no unmarked case.
78: 
79: The failure this prevents: an unconfirmed cause asserted as definitive, which the next
80: reader treats as settled and stops testing.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 2. COMMAND EVIDENCE
85: 
86: **A command counts as evidence only after its output and exit status have been read.**
87: 
88: - Never report output you did not see, or the output you *expected*.
89: - **Exit 0 with no output is a suspicious pass, not a pass.** A runner that failed to
90:   start, a script that no-oped on a symlinked path, a matcher that selected zero files,
91:   and a stale build that refused to run all exit 0 or print nothing.
92: - **Verify by content, not exit code.** Require the affirmative marker (`RESULT: PASSED`,
93:   the test count, the file listing), not merely the absence of a failure marker.
94: - Run focused checks during repair; before claiming completion **re-run the whole
95:   authoritative gate**. A focused pass is not a gate pass.
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## 3. THE FOUR WAYS A GREEN RUN LIES
100: 
101: 1. **It did not run.** Stale build, refused start, missing binary, guard clause, crashed
102:    before the first test body.
103: 2. **It ran on the wrong thing.** Wrong path, branch, or working directory; a symlink
104:    that resolved elsewhere; a filter that matched nothing. A search that returns nothing
105:    is not evidence of absence until you have confirmed it read the file: `grep` treats a
106:    source file holding a NUL byte as binary and prints nothing at all. Re-run with `-a`
107:    before concluding.
108: 3. **It ran on stale artifacts.** Cached output, an old bundle, pre-change fixtures, a
109:    metadata fingerprint that no longer attests its source.
110: 4. **It asserted nothing.** A test with no assertion, a mocked subject, an auto-updated
111:    snapshot, an empty parametrization.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 4. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL
116: 
117: **Before the fix, reproduce the exact failing symptom with the exact check you will use
118: to prove the fix.** A check that passed before your change and passes after it proves
119: nothing about your change. If reproducing is unsafe, say so and name what you used
120: instead.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 5. BASELINES
125: 
126: "No regressions" is a comparison, and a comparison needs a before.
127: 
128: 1. Capture the real starting numbers, pass/fail counts, timings, sizes, before
129:    changing anything.
130: 2. Re-run the **whole** gate afterwards, not the subset you were iterating on.
131: 3. Report the delta, including the parts that did not move.
132: 
133: Same for any performance claim: measure under stated conditions, report baseline and
134: delta. An unmeasured performance claim is not a caveat, it is a fabrication.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## 6. SHAPE-SPECIFIC PROOF
139: 
140: - **Filter or transform:** enumerate every in-scope variant *first*, process each, then
141:   rescan the whole surface for residue. The variants you never enumerated are the ones
142:   you missed.
143: - **Computed answer:** derive it a second way, independently, before writing the number.
144:   Re-reading your own arithmetic is not an independent derivation.
145: - **Exact artifact:** check filename, path, format and content shape directly. Having
146:   written it is not evidence it is there in the required shape.
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## 7. A FINDING IS A HYPOTHESIS
151: 
152: A sub-agent's "COMPLETE", a reviewer's "P0", a linter's error, a bot's suggestion: each
153: is a **claim to confirm against the real symptom**, not a fact to act on. Acting on an
154: unconfirmed finding produces a fix for a bug that was never there, plus a diff nobody
155: can explain. Confirming the symptom is
156: [`root-cause-and-debugging.md`](root-cause-and-debugging.md), and a delegate's return is
157: [`delegation-and-orchestration.md`](delegation-and-orchestration.md).
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 8. PROOF PLAN BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
162: 
163: For anything with a machine-checkable outcome, **before changing files**, convert the
164: acceptance criteria into 1–5 observable pass/fail checks. Each names the exact command
165: or inspection, the exact path/filename/format expected, and the boundary case it exposes.
166: 
167: Deciding what would count as proof *after* you have the result is how the result becomes
168: the standard.
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## 9. FINAL-STATE PROOF
173: 
174: Before any completion claim:
175: 
176: - [ ] Every required artifact exists **at its exact path** in the required format, verified by inspection, not by the fact that you wrote it.
177: - [ ] The §8 proof plan and the authoritative gate both pass **from the final state**, output and exit status read.
178: - [ ] The scoped diff contains no task-created residue, no scratch files, no debug
179:       output, no unrelated file.
180: - [ ] Any failing check keeps the completion claim blocked. Repair, or report the
181:       blocker with its evidence. There is no third option.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 10. CLOSE-OUT
186: 
187: Every substantive turn ends with an honest status. What it holds is listed once, in
188: [`communication-handoff.md`](communication-handoff.md) §1.
189: 
190: And plainly: **what is not done.** If tests fail, say so and show the output. If a step
191: was skipped, say it was skipped. If scope was left out, name it and why. Work that is
192: done and verified is stated plainly, without hedging. **The first report is the honest
193: one:** a claim that becomes accurate only under interrogation failed when it was
194: written, not when it was corrected. What is now the operator's to do is a separate
195: report, see [`communication-handoff.md`](communication-handoff.md) §1.
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 11. REASON FROM DATA, NOT FROM MEMORY
200: 
201: Two habits produce most of the claims that then need retracting:
202: 
203: **Reasoning from what the code probably does.** Open it. The cost of being wrong here
204: is not one wrong sentence, it is a fix built on a wrong model, which fails in a way
205: that looks like a different bug.
206: 
207: **Reasoning from what a document says the code does.** A README, a spec, a comment, and
208: a prior implementation summary are all claims about the code by someone who is not the
209: code. They are excellent for finding *where* to look and worthless as the final word on
210: *what happens*. Where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins and the doc is now a
211: defect.
212: 
213: Before the change, run the checks that decide whether it is the right change at all:
214: does something simpler already do this, what does it cost at runtime, who maintains it
215: after you, and is any of it outside the frozen scope.
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 12. SELF-CHECK
220: 
221: - [ ] Every load-bearing sentence is marked OBSERVED, DERIVED, or INFERRED.
222: - [ ] I read the output and exit status of every command I am citing.
223: - [ ] Checked the green run against the four failure modes in §3.
224: - [ ] A before-number exists for every "no regressions" and performance claim.
225: - [ ] The close-out says what failed and what is inferred, not only what worked.
226: - [ ] The close-out names any known residual risk the operator must weigh. It says "none known" when there is none.
227: - [ ] Every claim about behavior came from the code or a command, not from memory or a doc.
228: - [ ] Where a document and the code disagreed, I said so rather than trusting the document.
229: - [ ] Every receipt I cite could have come out differently if the claim were false, or it is marked inferred.
230: - [ ] I reproduced the failure with the same check that now proves the fix, or said why I could not.
231: - [ ] A filter enumerated its variants first, a computed answer was derived twice, an exact artifact was checked by name and shape.
232: - [ ] Every sub-agent, reviewer or tool finding I acted on was confirmed against the real symptom first.
233: - [ ] The proof plan existed before the first edit, and it passed from the final state with the scoped diff clean of residue.

157: [`delegation-and-orchestration.md`](delegation-and-orchestration.md).
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 8. PROOF PLAN BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
162: 
163: For anything with a machine-checkable outcome, **before changing files**, convert the
164: acceptance criteria into 1–5 observable pass/fail checks. Each names the exact command
165: or inspection, the exact path/filename/format expected, and the boundary case it exposes.
166: 
167: Deciding what would count as proof *after* you have the result is how the result becomes
168: the standard.
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## 9. FINAL-STATE PROOF
173: 
174: Before any completion claim:
175: 
176: - [ ] Every required artifact exists **at its exact path** in the required format, verified by inspection, not by the fact that you wrote it.
177: - [ ] The §8 proof plan and the authoritative gate both pass **from the final state**, output and exit status read.
178: - [ ] The scoped diff contains no task-created residue, no scratch files, no debug
179:       output, no unrelated file.
180: - [ ] Any failing check keeps the completion claim blocked. Repair, or report the
181:       blocker with its evidence. There is no third option.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 10. CLOSE-OUT
186: 
187: Every substantive turn ends with an honest status. What it holds is listed once, in
188: [`communication-handoff.md`](communication-handoff.md) §1.
189: 
190: And plainly: **what is not done.** If tests fail, say so and show the output. If a step
191: was skipped, say it was skipped. If scope was left out, name it and why. Work that is
192: done and verified is stated plainly, without hedging. **The first report is the honest
193: one:** a claim that becomes accurate only under interrogation failed when it was
194: written, not when it was corrected. What is now the operator's to do is a separate
195: report, see [`communication-handoff.md`](communication-handoff.md) §1.
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 11. REASON FROM DATA, NOT FROM MEMORY
200: 
201: Two habits produce most of the claims that then need retracting:
202: 
203: **Reasoning from what the code probably does.** Open it. The cost of being wrong here
204: is not one wrong sentence, it is a fix built on a wrong model, which fails in a way
205: that looks like a different bug.
206: 
207: **Reasoning from what a document says the code does.** A README, a spec, a comment, and
208: a prior implementation summary are all claims about the code by someone who is not the
209: code. They are excellent for finding *where* to look and worthless as the final word on
210: *what happens*. Where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins and the doc is now a
211: defect.
212: 
213: Before the change, run the checks that decide whether it is the right change at all:
214: does something simpler already do this, what does it cost at runtime, who maintains it
215: after you, and is any of it outside the frozen scope.
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 12. SELF-CHECK
220: 
221: - [ ] Every load-bearing sentence is marked OBSERVED, DERIVED, or INFERRED.
222: - [ ] I read the output and exit status of every command I am citing.
223: - [ ] Checked the green run against the four failure modes in §3.
224: - [ ] A before-number exists for every "no regressions" and performance claim.
225: - [ ] The close-out says what failed and what is inferred, not only what worked.
226: - [ ] The close-out names any known residual risk the operator must weigh. It says "none known" when there is none.
227: - [ ] Every claim about behavior came from the code or a command, not from memory or a doc.
228: - [ ] Where a document and the code disagreed, I said so rather than trusting the document.
229: - [ ] Every receipt I cite could have come out differently if the claim were false, or it is marked inferred.
230: - [ ] I reproduced the failure with the same check that now proves the fix, or said why I could not.
231: - [ ] A filter enumerated its variants first, a computed answer was derived twice, an exact artifact was checked by name and shape.
232: - [ ] Every sub-agent, reviewer or tool finding I acted on was confirmed against the real symptom first.
233: - [ ] The proof plan existed before the first edit, and it passed from the final state with the scoped diff clean of residue.
